idea: Capacity constraints turn pathfinding into a flow problem. Reverse residual arcs let later augmentations undo earlier choices.
steps: Construct an independent residual/reverse pair for every input edge.
Use BFS levels and blocking-flow DFS until the sink is unreachable.
Find the reachable residual side; outgoing original capacities form the minimum cut.
example: s→a capacity 7 and a→t capacity 4 carry at most 4 units; the final cut has capacity 4.
concepts: How much additional flow an arc can carry.
Allows existing flow to be canceled when rerouting.
A cut with capacity equal to the feasible flow certifies optimality.
question: Can opposite input edges share the same reverse arc?
answer: No. Original antiparallel and parallel edges need separate residual pairs to preserve capacities and flow accounting.
challenge: Run Parallel pipes and verify conservation at a.
cost: Dinic has a general O(V²E) bound; the bounded demo records one trace per BFS phase.
